subject: PHI routing and deployment constraints for BlueHealth - next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: PHI routing and deployment constraints — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Cassie — good conversation. I wanted to recap the key points from our discovery and lay out clear next steps so your security and procurement teams have what they need to evaluate Redwood.

Recap (from our call):
- BlueHealth will be sending real patient identifiers and clinical notes into the model for triage/summary workflows (ePHI).
- Primary concerns: BAA availability, where ePHI might be persisted (logs/analytics/embeddings), and which deployment modes are acceptable under your policies.
- You asked about our SOC 2 status and whether we can support private networking / on-prem options for regulated workloads.

What Redwood can offer (brief):
- Hosted API: fastest route, but not typically used for ePHI unless paired with a dedicated, VPC-connected environment and explicit logging controls under contract.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with data isolation and optional VPC peering — supports disabling analytics/token retention; commonly used for customers who want strong isolation but prefer managed infra.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-controlled network and optional air-gapped installs — recommended when policy requires the customer to control all network egress and KMS.

Immediate asks / next steps I can action:
1) I will send our vendor security questionnaire backfilled and a draft BAA for your counsel to review (attached).
2) Can you confirm the PHI surface (exact fields/types): are you sending images, raw DICOMs, or only structured/unstructured text and identifiers? This will affect our recommended deployment and retention settings.
3) Security team: please share any must-have controls (e.g., inability to persist embeddings, requirement for HSM-backed keys, SOC 2 scope items).
4) If procurement needs an initial cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private, let me know target RPS/throughput and retention windows; I’ll loop infra for a sizing + cost workbook.

Attachments: BlueHealth_Vendor_Sec_Questionnaire.xlsx (placeholder), redwood_baa_draft.pdf (draft), initial_scope_template.xlsx

I’ll follow up with answers to your SOC 2 question and some configuration notes in the next email.

Best,

From: Cassie Turner <cassie.turner@bluehealth.ai>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI routing and deployment constraints — follow-up and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the detailed recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) PHI surface: Initially it will be unstructured clinical notes and a handful of identifiers (MRN, DOB). No images or DICOMs in scope for MVP.
2) Retention policy: We cannot allow persistent storage of ePHI outside of our control. Embeddings derived from ePHI are considered ePHI for our policy (so they must not be retained by the vendor).
3) Keys: We prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for any production Private deployments; for Dedicated, HSM-backed provider KMS is acceptable if we have contractual guarantees and key rotation policies documented.
4) SOC 2: please confirm your current SOC 2 Type (I/II) and most recent audit date. Also include which systems are in-scope (control tower / control plane / data plane separation).

Security team (security@bluehealth.ai) — feel free to add specifics, especially re: logging/alerting and audit log retention.

Procurement — we’ll need a redlined BAA and an initial cost comparison for Dedicated vs Private to decide which path to move forward.

Regards,
Cassie Turner
Head of IT Security | BlueHealth Diagnostics
cassie.turner@bluehealth.ai

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI routing and deployment constraints — follow-up and next steps

Cassie — great, thanks for confirming the PHI surface and constraints. A few concrete notes inline and what I’ll produce this morning:

SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II (report issued 2025-11). I will attach the SOC 2 cover letter and provide a redacted report under an NDA if you require the full report. In-scope: control plane and data plane are separated; data plane for Hosted API is multi-tenant unless you opt into Dedicated/Private.

Embeddings/retention: We support a no-retention mode for Dedicated and Private deployments — embeddings and model outputs can be marked non-persistent. For Hosted API, we can provide session-level isolation and limited retention under a contractual data processing addendum, but generally we advise Dedicated or Private if your policy treats embeddings as ePHI.

KMS: Private (on-prem or VPC with customer KMS) supports BYOK/HSM. For Dedicated, we offer provider-managed HSM-backed keys with written key rotation and access controls in the BAA + KM integration appendix.

Deliverables I’ll send within the hour:
- Completed vendor sec questionnaire (answers inline)
- Draft BAA (redwood_baa_draft.pdf)
- Short note comparing Dedicated vs Private for PHI (including typical provisioning timelines)

Next commercial step: Lauren, can you prepare a Dedicated vs Private estimate (linked workbook attached) and flag any lead-times for Private (on-prem) installs? Ben/Karthik — please advise on the infra sizing assumptions I should pass to procurement (target throughput: 30 RPS, average 512 tokens per call; SLA 99.9).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our infra lead to validate the non-retention controls and key management setup.

Thanks,
Jordan
